title: Proper pushforward preserves ambient coproducts on the constructible finite-Tor localizing hull over a qcqs base
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a fixed algebraic closure, and an admissible commutative condensed ring $\Lambda$: a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$, or $\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with exactly the discrete or induced $\ell$-adic topological condensed-ring convention of [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ and $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T})$, the ordinary unbounded module-object derived category [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], with the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Use the finite constant scalar-model constructibility and finite Tor amplitude of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Let $S$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme, $q:Y\to S$ proper and $f:X\to Y$ proper. Write $\mathcal L_X=\operatorname{Loc}(\mathrm D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X,\Lambda))$ for the full replete triangulated hull closed under small coproducts in $D_X$ [sk-def-localizing-closure]. For every small set $I$ and every family $(L_t)_{t\in I}$ in $\mathcal L_X$, the canonical map induced by the coprojections
$$\bigoplus_{t\in I}Rf_*L_t\longrightarrow Rf_*\left(\bigoplus_{t\in I}L_t\right)$$
is an isomorphism in $D_Y$. Both coproducts are ambient ordinary derived-category coproducts in the fixed indexing universe, including the empty family. No common cohomological bounds on the family and no derived completeness of its sum are assumed. No field, characteristic, Noetherian or finite-dimensional-base hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: (2) Isomorphism, first paragraph: the proper direct image used in the compactification candidate preserves direct sums on the localizing hull. Agent formulation in the qcqs scope of det-sf-comp-coherence-cocycle; not an attribution of this full coefficient/ambient-category statement to a narrower source theorem.

proof.text: For $T=X,Y$, the abelian sheaf category on the chosen small pro-étale site is closed symmetric monoidal Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed], applied to $\Ab$ with its usual tensor product. Its tensor is additive. The module-object theorem [lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck] therefore makes $\mathcal A_T=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T}$ Grothendieck abelian. The termwise coproduct theorem [lem-kun-grothendieck-derived-coproducts] supplies all the ambient derived coproducts in the fixed universe, including the empty coproduct.

Coproducts in $\mathcal A_T$ are exact: they are filtered colimits of finite direct sums, and filtered colimits are exact by the Grothendieck property established in Step 1. Consequently kernels, images and cokernels in a termwise sum of complexes are the sums of the corresponding kernels, images and cokernels. Thus $H^n(\bigoplus_t C_t)=\bigoplus_tH^n(C_t)$, naturally with the specified coprojections. The kernel/cokernel formulas of [def-kun-truncations] similarly identify $\bigoplus_t\tau_{\geq a}C_t$ with $\tau_{\geq a}(\bigoplus_t C_t)$ and identify the sum of the canonical truncation maps with the canonical truncation map of the sum. The termwise-derived-coproduct theorem makes these identities valid in $D_T$ for unbounded families.

source.place: (2), first paragraph: cohomology and good truncations of ambient sums

proof.text:
Properness makes $f$ finite type, hence quasi-compact by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and separated, hence quasi-separated by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. For every integer $a$, [lem-sfb-adic-proper-bounded-below-coproducts] therefore applies to the family $(\tau_{\geq a}L_t)_t$: all its terms have zero cohomology below the SAME $a$. It gives an invertible canonical comparison
$$\beta_a:\bigoplus_tRf_*\tau_{\geq a}L_t\longrightarrow Rf_*\bigl(\bigoplus_t\tau_{\geq a}L_t\bigr).$$
That theorem accepts any commutative condensed coefficient ring and any small indexing type, so it applies to every coefficient in the statement, including the empty family.

source.place: Lemma 5.3(1); passage to arbitrary coproducts by finite partial sums

proof.text:
Choose $c$ from [lem-sfb-qcqs-proper-hull-tail-bound]. Fix an output degree $n$ and set $a=n-c$. For every $K\in\mathcal L_X$, use the canonical triangle
$$\tau_{<a}K\longrightarrow K\xrightarrow{\pi_K}\tau_{\geq a}K\longrightarrow(\tau_{<a}K)[1]$$
of the standard t-structure. The actual total right derived functor is triangulated by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. In its image triangle the tail estimate kills $H^n$ AND $H^{n+1}$ of the first term, since both degrees are at least $a+c=n$. Exactness of the cohomology sequence therefore gives an isomorphism $H^n(Rf_*\pi_K)$. This applies to each $L_t$ and to $K=\bigoplus_tL_t$, because the defining ambient localizing closure contains that sum. It does not require $\tau_{\geq a}K$ or $\tau_{<a}K$ to belong to the hull.

source.place: (2), first paragraph: uniform tail removal before applying direct-sum continuity

proof.text: Write $\beta:\bigoplus_tRf_*L_t\to Rf_*(\bigoplus_tL_t)$ for the required comparison. The square with top row $\beta$, bottom row $\beta_a$, and vertical arrows induced by the $\pi_{L_t}$ commutes: precompose either composite with the $t$-th coprojection and, after the Step 2 identification, both become $Rf_*(\pi_{\bigoplus_s L_s}\circ\iota_t)=Rf_*((\tau_{\geq a}\iota_t)\circ\pi_{L_t})$, using naturality of $\pi$. Step 2 identifies its lower right vertex with $Rf_*\tau_{\geq a}(\bigoplus_tL_t)$ and its right vertical map with $Rf_*\pi_{\bigoplus_tL_t}$. After $H^n$, Step 4 makes the right vertical map invertible; Step 2 and the individual instances of Step 4 make the left vertical map invertible. Step 3 makes the bottom map invertible. The commutative square now makes $H^n(\beta)$ invertible. As $n$ was arbitrary, [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] proves that $\beta$ is an isomorphism in the ambient $D_Y$.

source.place: (2), first paragraph: natural coproduct comparison detected degree by degree

proof.text: For $I=\varnothing$, the ambient sum is zero and the triangulated $Rf_*$ sends zero to zero, so the same canonical comparison is invertible. Each degree used its own cutoff $a=n-c$; the original family was never assigned a common cohomological bound. All constructions used ordinary ambient sums and good truncations, so no completeness assertion about the sum was used.

Step 3: I checked every hypothesis of lem-sfb-adic-proper-bounded-below-coproducts: a qcqs map via finite type plus separated⇒qs, any condensed ring, the common bound a, and the empty I. The adic case is plausible and matches the existing field versions lem-sfb-adic-proper-truncation-bound and det-sf-comp-continuous-algcl-lower-tail. It generalizes those nodes and is not a duplicate.
